reason: The sources provide over a dozen cross-verified facts across independent sites documenting Aeolis Mons, Gale Crater, and Curiosity's ascent.
story: At the center of Mars's 154-kilometer-wide Gale Crater sits Aeolis Mons, an enormous mountain known informally to NASA as Mount Sharp. Rising 5.5 kilometers (18,000 feet) above the crater floor, this towering peak rises higher than Mount Rainier stands above Seattle and possesses a greater base-to-peak rise than Mount Everest. Unlike volcanic peaks, Aeolis Mons is an immense stack of sedimentary rock, deposited billions of years ago when Gale Crater held lakes and streams for thousands to millions of years, before Martian winds eroded the surrounding basin into an isolated mountain. In August 2012, NASA landed Curiosity, a car-sized rover carrying ten scientific instruments, on the crater floor. Equipped with cameras and a rock drill, Curiosity has spent over a decade slowly crawling up the mountain's layered slopes, decoding how an ancient wet, potentially habitable Martian environment dried out into a barren desert.
angle: Inside a Martian crater the size of Connecticut and Rhode Island sits a mountain taller from base to peak than Mount Everest—and a lone car-sized robot has spent over a decade climbing its ancient, water-carved layers.

claims.claim: Aeolis Mons forms the central peak inside Gale Crater on Mars.
Gale Crater spans 154 kilometers in diameter.
Aeolis Mons rises 5.5 kilometers (18,000 feet) above the crater floor.
NASA informally nicknamed the central peak Mount Sharp.
The informal name Mount Sharp honors American geologist Robert P. Sharp.
Aeolis Mons is an eroded mound of sedimentary layers.
An ancient lake basin existed inside Gale Crater for thousands to millions of years.
Wind-driven erosion exhumed the sedimentary layers that formed the mountain.
The sedimentary strata of Mount Sharp record the transition of Mars from an ancient wet climate to a dry environment.
NASA's Curiosity rover landed inside Gale Crater in August 2012.
Curiosity targeted a refined landing ellipse measuring 20 by 7 kilometers.
The Curiosity rover is the size of a car.
Curiosity was equipped with 10 scientific instruments.
Curiosity's prime mission includes investigating whether Gale Crater could have supported microbial life.
Curiosity has been ascending and exploring the slopes of Mount Sharp.
Curiosity uses a drill on its robotic arm to sample powdered rock.
Organic chemicals were detected in powder drilled from Gale Crater rocks.
Orbital observations detected clay and sulfate minerals in Gale Crater before the landing.

disputed: Landing calendar date: North American time zones record the landing on the evening of August 5, 2012, whereas UTC and European time zones record August 6, 2012. A script should cite 'August 2012' or specify the time zone.

Origin of lower sedimentary layers: Sources note an ongoing scientific debate over whether katabatic wind deposition or lakebed sedimentation played the dominant role in forming the lowest mound layers. A script should frame the lakebed origin as an evidence-supported interpretation.

Source of organic molecules: Sources disagree on whether organic compounds detected by Curiosity originated from biological activity, abiotic water-rock chemistry, or interplanetary dust and meteorites. A script should describe them strictly as organic building blocks rather than proof of life.
